headline: THE THREE ROUND-6 BLOCKERS ARE ALL GENUINELY CLOSED, each reproduced by this reviewer on the shipped CLI, and the KIND TEST is a COMPLETE partition over filesystem entry types rather than another enumeration - twenty-one shapes swept, every non-regular-file entry fails closed. The item fails AGAIN on the same class it was told to fix: FOUR measured-false checkable sentences, two of them shipping in eight engine copies and one of them written INTO the spec's acceptance criterion this round, plus one diagnosability defect in the code. The worst is the third recurrence of the availability-cost understatement that R5-B3(c) already blocked: the manifest says the emacs lock is THE ONE availability regression this pass accepts, and measurement finds FOURTEEN shapes that rendered at b1d6894 and stand the section down at a6b6316, of which ten cannot lose a record at all - including an `archive/` subdirectory, which round 6's own spec and table DECLARED as a supported shape.

must_fix_before_live.summary: "THE EMACS LOCK IS THE ONE AVAILABILITY REGRESSION THIS PASS ACCEPTS" (manifest.json:193) is FALSE BY MEASUREMENT. The reviewer resolved the round-6 accounted read from git (b1d6894:.warp/metrics_read_accounting.py) and ran both versions over twenty-one seeded shapes: FOURTEEN entries that made the read AFFIRM COMPLETE at round 6 leave it INCOMPLETE at round 7. Ten of the fourteen cannot lose a record under either version, so they are PURE availability loss with zero correctness gain: an EMPTY .gitkeep directory, an EMPTY archive/, a .gitkeep symlinked to a NON-record file, a dangling .gitkeep symlink, a symlink LOOP named .gitkeep, a second emacs lock shape (.#other), a skip-named FIFO, a skip-named UNIX SOCKET, and a .gitkeep symlinked to /dev/null. THE ONE THAT MATTERS IS archive/: round 6 shipped it as a DECLARED row ('an operator's archive of superseded records') in the table and in the spec's AC3 text, so an adopter who followed the declaration now has the whole section stood down. The manifest even attaches the distinguishing clause 'and which round 6 rendered' to the emacs lock alone, when every one of the eight shapes in its own list rendered at round 6. Round 5 blocked this item for understating the availability cost of option A (R5-B3(c)); round 6's note 2 restated it; this is the third time. THE FIX IS THE SENTENCE, NOT THE CODE: state that every skip-named non-regular-file entry that round 6 dismissed now stands the section down, and name archive/ as the withdrawn declaration it is.

must_fix_before_live.severity: blocking on honesty, and it is IN THE SPEC
must_fix_before_live.summary: The property the pass claims to have closed is BROADER THAN THE KIND TEST, and the gap is neither closed nor declared. Two sentences: .warp/metrics_read_accounting.py:41 'Nothing that could CONTAIN or RESOLVE TO a record is skipped by name (_skippable_entry)' (eight shipped copies: root, plugin/templates, six packs) and specs/WARP-1210-the-support-numbers.md:72-73 'Only a REGULAR FILE may be skipped that way; anything that could hold or resolve to a record leaves the read INCOMPLETE'. MEASURED FALSE TWICE: (a) a REGULAR FILE named .gitkeep whose bytes ARE a record renders, is skipped by name, and the read affirms COMPLETE; (b) a HARDLINK named .gitkeep to a real record's inode does the same - the record's bytes sit in the store under a dismissed name with no indirection at all, which is a strictly stronger version of the '.gitkeep symlinked to a real record' loss the pass exists to close, and a hardlink is a regular file so _skippable_entry cannot see it. The manifest's residual list (manifest.json:193) says 'every one is measured rather than described' and does not contain either shape. The KIND rule is defensible and the reviewer does not ask for it to change; what must change is a sentence that claims a content-and-target property the code does not enforce, written into an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION this round.

must_fix_before_live.severity: blocking on honesty, and this pass DELETED the correct qualifier
must_fix_before_live.summary: .warp/metrics_read_accounting.py:203-205 (eight copies): 'anything else - a subdirectory, a symlink, a FIFO, another suffix, a case variant - is UNACCOUNTED and leaves the read INCOMPLETE'. MEASURED FALSE for a symlink: a symlink named INC-2.yaml resolving to a real record is CONSUMED (two records read where the seed writes one) and the read affirms COMPLETE, because the consume branch at line 237 asks os.path.isfile, which FOLLOWS the link. Round 6's sentence at the same place said 'a symlink that does not resolve', which was CORRECT; this pass removed the qualifier while rewriting the paragraph, so the pass whose mandate was prose accuracy made this sentence LESS accurate. The same overstatement rides in manifest.json:194 judgment (c), 'A SYMLINK IS NEVER A REGULAR FILE here whatever it resolves to', and in the capability entry ('a SYMLINK IS NEVER ONE whatever it resolves to'): true in the skip branch only. Worse for the stated reasoning - the TOCTOU argument in _skippable_entry's docstring ('what a link resolves to can change after the check, so a rule that trusted the target would be deciding on a fact it does not hold') applies verbatim to the consume branch, which trusts the target.

must_fix_before_live.severity: blocking, and this half is a DEFECT rather than prose
must_fix_before_live.summary: THE TWO SHAPES R6-B2(a) WAS ABOUT ARE MISNAMED IN THE STAND-DOWN A HUMAN READS. Measured on the shipped code: '.gitkeep' symlinked to a real record is reported as '.gitkeep (a file this reader does not consume)' and 'archive' symlinked to a directory of records as 'archive (a directory)'. _entry_kind (.warp/metrics_read_accounting.py:180-192) never says 'a symlink' unless the link DANGLES, so the fact that made the entry unaccountable is invisible, and the reader calls 'a file' an entry _skippable_entry has just decided is NOT a regular file. An operator sees a name the table explicitly declares skippable, reported as an unaccounted file, and cannot act on it - which is exactly what the function's own docstring says it exists to prevent ('the reader has to say WHAT it could not account for, or a human cannot act on the stand-down', lines 181-182). The manifest then enumerates the naming as though it were complete for all eight shapes - 'the entry named for WHAT IT IS (a directory / a symlink that does not resolve / an entry that is neither a regular file nor a directory)' (manifest.json:48) - while the assertion at scripts/selftest.py:16960-16964 checks only THREE of the eight, and the two it does not check are the two that contradict the enumeration. A property exhibited over the convenient three, exactly the shape four prior reviews named.

spec_edit_ruling: THE SPEC EDIT IS NOT A WEAKENING IN THE CORRECTNESS DIRECTION, and the reviewer went looking for one. Removing the `archive` row is a GENUINE narrowing: with the kind test in place the row could only ever match a REGULAR FILE named `archive`, while its declared reason ('an operator's archive of superseded records') describes a directory, so the row would have been a false declaration - and the kind test alone already closes the measured loss, so the removal is redundant hardening rather than a dodge of a failing assertion. Every other AC3 change makes the criterion STRICTER (entries -> REGULAR FILES; the new 'THE RULE MATCHES REGULAR FILES ONLY' sentence; the measured figures corrected from twelve to seventeen plus eight), and the observability block was strengthened from a basis nobody renders to all three surfaces. TWO THINGS THE OWNER SHOULD SEE ANYWAY. FIRST, the exception list was WIDENED by eight names (.keep, .gitattributes, .swo, .orig, .rej, .bak, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini) in the author's own acceptance criterion, on the strength of a review NOTE rather than an owner decision; the correctness risk is bounded by suffix-first, so this is an availability/honesty trade rather than a hazard, but the trade is the owner's to make since he approved the approach on a stated cost. SECOND, and this is the cardinal risk landing in a different form than expected: the edit wrote a NEW UNTRUE checkable sentence into the criterion itself (R7-B2, specs/WARP-1210-the-support-numbers.md:72-73 and 176-177). An acceptance criterion that claims a property the implementation does not have is worse than one that was merely narrowed, because every later round will audit against it.
notes: Ranked by six-month impact. 1. THE LOOP MEASURES ARE NOW SILENTLY LOCALE-DEPENDENT, which the guard's declaration does not say. Measured on the shipped CLI over one three-event stream that is VALID UTF-8 with a single non-ASCII character: under a true ASCII locale (LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0) all four surfaces report events_total 2 and gate pass rate 1.0, and under C.UTF-8 the same bytes report events_total 3 and gate pass rate 0.667. Round 6 exited 1 on that stream, so the manifest's 'the only stream the change can move is one that produced nothing at all before' survives in the LETTER - but the loop measures can now be derived from a stream read in PART, which is the exact thing this item's governing rule exists to forbid one module over, and the two populations are NOT the same: the pre-existing skip drops a line that does not PARSE, while the new one drops a line that DOES parse (json.loads accepts a lone surrogate, which is precisely why the explicit encode check is load-bearing). The support section names UNREADABLE_EVENT_STREAM on every surface, which is what keeps this a note rather than a blocker. Declare the locale dependence and the parse/encode distinction, or say the loop numbers are lower bounds when the support pass has stood the stream down. 2. 'a line carrying such a byte is SKIPPED exactly as an unparseable line has always been skipped' (manifest.json:112) is not the same PATH: load() now holds three try blocks and four continue statements, and the encode check is its own try/except ahead of json.loads. Outcome-equivalent, path-distinct, and necessarily so. 3. 'The skipped-entry surfacing adds NO line, NO card and NO key on a store that holds only records' (manifest.json:156) is FALSE for the machine surface, measured by running metrics.py --json at b1d6894 and at a6b6316 over the SAME committed stream: the round-7 output gains exactly one line, `"read_skipped": [],`. Text and HTML are byte-identical, so 'NO line, NO card' is true. The backing assertion says the honest thing ('an empty read_skipped', scripts/selftest.py:17224) and its own next clause asserts `"read_skipped" in SUPPORT_JSON_VERDICT`, i.e. the key IS there - while the comment above it at scripts/selftest.py:17221 repeats 'no key'. This is the overstatement pattern in miniature: the manifest upgraded 'empty' to 'absent'. 4. THE HEADROOM RANKING IS WRONG. 'the tightest is now the ACCOUNTED READ at 299 of 300, then the evidence readers at 297 of 300 and the shape readers at 298 of 300' (manifest.json:196) ranks 297 ahead of 298; measured, the order after the accounted read is the SHAPE readers (298, two lines) then the evidence readers (297, three lines). The seam itself is REAL rather than hand-waved: the declared skip rule (the table, _SUPPORT_SKIP_MATCH, store_skip_reason and _skippable_entry, lines 101-158) is about 58 lines with exactly one call site at line 239, so the split would leave the accounted read near 241, and the stated reason for deferring it (a tenth engine file across eight copies for a fifteen-row table) is honest. 5. Number-neutrality is ASSERTED over one fixture (this repository's stream) and true as a PROPERTY only by argument; the reviewer verified the argument holds, but under this item's own standard the universal sentence wants either an assertion over an adversarial stream or a narrower sentence. 6. The right-schema receipt forgery remains the ceiling on this item's honesty and is correctly ranked first in the assumptions; W11 still owns it. 7. 2571 lines gate-ungoverned, arithmetic verified against the measured counts (435+752+299+126+298+297+364) and against round 6's 2510 (425+744+275+126+298+297+345); the figure is exact and the declaration is honest. 8. Carried and unfixed, correctly declared: support_json(None) raises, the whitespace-only event type divergence, withheld naming keys whose content reappears in named_inputs, support_share's 300 percent, the module-global vocabulary cache, only the support section honouring root.

disposition: NOT LANDED. Nothing needs redesigning and the reviewer says so for the fourth consecutive round: the completeness default holds, the KIND test is a complete partition over entry types rather than another list of names, all three round-6 blockers are closed and each was reproduced here on the shipped CLI. What fails is the same class the pass was explicitly told to close, and the pass closed it in most places while opening it in four new ones - two of them in the ENGINE's eight copies and one of them written INTO the acceptance criterion, where it will be audited against forever. THE METHOD LESSON THIS ROUND ADDS, because 'a sentence that makes a checkable claim must be backed by an assertion' was necessary and not sufficient: EVERY SENTENCE CONTAINING THE WORDS 'ONE', 'ONLY', 'NEVER', 'ANYTHING' OR 'NOTHING' IS A UNIVERSAL QUANTIFIER, AND A UNIVERSAL WANTS AN ENUMERATION OF ITS DOMAIN BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN, NOT AN ASSERTION OVER THE THREE MEMBERS THAT WERE CONVENIENT. Each of R7-B1 through R7-B4 is a universal ('the ONE availability regression', 'NOTHING that could contain or resolve to a record', 'ANYTHING else ... is UNACCOUNTED', 'named for WHAT IT IS') whose domain the author never enumerated, and in every case the counter-example was reachable in under a minute with a temporary directory and the git-resolved predecessor. The remaining work is one to two hours and is almost entirely sentences: correct the availability declaration to name every shape round 6 rendered and withdraw archive/ explicitly, restate the contain-or-resolve claim as the KIND rule it actually is and declare the hardlink and record-bearing-regular-file residual, restore the 'that does not resolve' qualifier the pass deleted, and teach _entry_kind to say 'a symlink' before it says what the link resolves to - that last one being the only code change, and the only finding here that a human operator would ever feel.
